fixtures: SwiftUI sources and a coverage report copied into data/. Runs are read-only, so changes are shown in the answer rather than written.

evals.name: blank-pill-on-launch
evals.prompt: On cold launch the app sometimes shows a tiny blank white rounded rectangle over a dimmed window instead of the project details; quitting and reopening usually fixes it. The code is in data/swiftui-projects/. Fix it, and tell me what else in these files will bite us.
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis: .sheet(isPresented:) presents while repo.project(for:) is still nil because refresh() has not loaded (or failed silently), so SwiftUI shows an empty view as a blank pill. Fix: .sheet(item:) with an Identifiable Project, set only once the store is ready, and give the repository an explicit LoadState (idle/loading/loaded/failed) with isReady instead of projects = [] plus isLoading. Also: try? in refresh() and in the Archive button swallow errors, which belong in view-model state the view shows; archivingIDs and the selection are business state that belongs in a @MainActor @Observable view model, not @State; project(for:) matching id || name is an identity seam: pick the canonical id (team/name) everywhere, including what is persisted in @AppStorage (it stores project.name today); ProjectRepository.shared and ProjectAPI.shared should be injected through a protocol with a default init argument so the view model is testable.
assertions: Explains the blank pill as .sheet(isPresented:) presenting an empty view while the project lookup is nil before the data has loaded
Replaces .sheet(isPresented:) with .sheet(item:) bound to an optional Identifiable project
Models the repository's loading lifecycle explicitly (an idle/loading/loaded/failed state with an isReady check) instead of projects = [] plus isLoading, and only presents the sheet once ready
Flags the try? in the Archive button action (and in refresh) and says the error must land in state the view displays, not be swallowed
Says archivingIDs (and the selection) are business state that belongs in a @MainActor @Observable view model, not @State
Flags the id || name lookup as an identity problem and makes the canonical id the only key, including the value stored in @AppStorage
Says the direct ProjectRepository.shared / ProjectAPI.shared use should become protocol-based injection with the singleton as an init default

evals.name: open-in-terminal-closure
evals.prompt: Implement the Open in Terminal TODO in data/WorkspaceViewModel.swift.
evals.expected_output: Calls NSWorkspace.shared.open([folder], withApplicationAt: Terminal's URL, configuration:, completionHandler:) with a completion closure explicitly marked @Sendable (capturing what it needs, e.g. [weak self]), because this API calls back on a background queue (com.apple.launchservices.open-queue) and a closure written inside a @MainActor type would otherwise inherit main-actor isolation and crash on entry. Inside, it hops back with Task { @MainActor in ... } to set errorMessage. It explains why the @Sendable is required and that the inner Task hop alone does not prevent the crash.
assertions: The completionHandler closure is explicitly annotated @Sendable
Hops back to the main actor (Task { @MainActor in ... }) before setting errorMessage
Explains that the closure would otherwise inherit @MainActor isolation and crash when NSWorkspace calls it on a background queue
Says the inner Task { @MainActor in } hop alone does not protect against the crash, because the isolation check fires when the closure is entered

evals.name: coverage-plan
evals.prompt: Our SwiftUI app's coverage is terrible; data/coverage-report.txt has the numbers. Give me the plan to fix it: what to target and in what order.
evals.expected_output: Targets by layer: services and view models 80-95%, pure utilities 95-100%, views 10-20%, overall 60-75%; the low number is uncovered services and view models, not the views. Order: audit, test services and utilities first; pure extractions out of the views (escapeForShell, score/filter, LogLineParser) committed as test:; then protocol + DI one service at a time, persistence first (BoardPersistence, which is writing test cards into the real board.json), via a protocol and an init default argument, committed as refactor:; then view model extraction (CardEditorView's @State form state); ViewInspector for the thin view residue; snapshot tests last. Refactor work and coverage work go in separate plans and separate PRs, never mixed. BoardViewTests redefining Card and Column locally is a coupling red flag.
assertions: Gives coverage targets by layer, with views around 10-20% and overall around 60-75%
Says the problem is uncovered services and view models, not the SwiftUI views
Puts BoardPersistence first among the DI work, because tests are writing into the real board.json
Plans pure extractions of escapeForShell, the card scoring and LogLineParser into standalone types, each tested on its own
Commits pure extractions as test: and protocol/DI introductions as refactor:
Keeps refactor work and coverage (test-adding) work in separate plans or PRs, never mixed
Introduces DI through a protocol and an init default argument such as init(persistence: any BoardPersistenceProtocol = BoardPersistence.shared)
Puts ViewInspector tests for the remaining views near the end and snapshot tests last
